description: The children's department of Pärnu's main library has picture books, board games and children's magazines, plus regular events and reading sessions. It is a free, warm and calm place to read with a toddler on a cold or rainy day.
tips: The library is closed on the last Friday of every month (internal working day).

price.note: Free; library card is free.

hours: Tue-Fri 10:00-19:00, Sat 10:00-15:00; Jun-Aug weekdays 10:00-18:00; closed Sun-Mon and the last Friday of the month
transport: Central Pärnu, walking distance from the old town

parkingInfo.note: Pärnu city-centre paid zone (since 1 Jun 2026): Mon-Fri 8-18, Sat 8-15, EUR 2/h or EUR 10/24h; Sundays and public holidays free; first 60 min free with a parking disc.

name: Pärnu Skypark
description: A trampoline and play centre inside the Kaubamajakas shopping centre with jumping, climbing and active play zones and a cheaper toddler ticket. It is Pärnu's main indoor play option, best on weekday mornings when it is quieter for little ones.
tips: Go Monday-Thursday when the toddler ticket is cheaper (EUR 6) and the hall is calmer; bring grip socks.

price.note: Toddler ticket EUR 6 Mon-Thu, EUR 8 Fri-Sun; regular day ticket EUR 11 Mon-Thu, EUR 13 Fri-Sun/school holidays; accompanying adult EUR 2.

transport: City buses to Kaubamajakas

parkingInfo.note: Large shopping-centre car park.

name: Pernova Nature House
description: A three-floor family nature centre with stuffed Estonian forest animals and birds, a winter garden, a film-and-sound cave and a dome cinema. Toddlers enjoy pointing at the animals and the greenery; the planetarium shows suit slightly older children better.
tips: Last entry is 60 minutes before closing; the centre is usually closed on Sundays outside summer.

price.note: Last published prices (may be outdated): adult EUR 11, pupils/students/seniors EUR 8, children 4-7 EUR 4, under 3 free, family EUR 30 (2 adults + minor children). Day ticket includes planetarium shows.

transport: City buses along Tammsaare pst

name: Haapsalu Episcopal Castle
description: A medieval castle ruin with a free, grassy castle park that is great for running around, plus a museum in the restored part of the castle. Children aged 0-8 get into the museum free, though steep stairs and narrow passages mean a carrier is easier than a stroller inside.
tips: The castle grounds are free all year, so you can just picnic and let your toddler roam without buying a ticket.

price.note: Museum: adult EUR 12, concession EUR 8, family EUR 28 (up to 2 adults + their children under 18). Children 0-8 free. Castle grounds free.

hours: Jun-Aug daily 10:00-18:00; Sep-May reduced days (closed Mon-Tue) - check the website; ticket office closes 30 min earlier
transport: Walk from Haapsalu bus station (about 15 min)

parkingInfo.note: Haapsalu town centre has municipal paid parking in places; check signs.

name: Haapsalu Railway and Communications Museum
description: The museum fills the long, ornate former Haapsalu railway station, and old locomotives and carriages stand on the tracks outside. Train-loving toddlers enjoy seeing the engines up close, and the long covered platform is good for a stroller walk.
tips: The building is also Haapsalu's bus station, so it is easy to reach without a car.

price.note: Listed as EUR 6 / EUR 5 (full / reduced); child prices not confirmed.

transport: Haapsalu bus station is in the same building

parkingInfo.note: Parking at the station / bus terminal area.

name: Aafrika Beach Playground and Promenade
description: Haapsalu's best-loved playground sits at the start of the seaside promenade, with restored wooden sculptures and the town's only bird-watching tower. The flat promenade is ideal for a stroller walk, and the Kuursaal summer café is close by.
tips: Walk the promenade to its far end, where there is a second, wheelchair-accessible playground.

price.note: Free.

transport: Walk from the castle / old town (about 10 min)

name: Paralepa Beach
description: Haapsalu's main sandy swimming beach, backed by pine forest, with a children's playground, changing cabins and portable toilets. The water is fairly shallow and calm, and lifeguards are on duty in summer.
tips: For a proper shower and flush toilet, use the paid facilities at Paralepa Camping or the Fra Mare spa hotel next door.

price.note: Free.

hours: Open all the time; official season 1 Jun-31 Aug with lifeguards daily 10:00-22:00
transport: About 2 km west of Haapsalu centre; walk or cycle along the coast

name: Kuressaare Episcopal Castle (Saaremaa Museum)
description: The best-preserved medieval castle in the Baltics, surrounded by a moat, ramparts and park, houses the Saaremaa Museum. Toddlers enjoy the towers, cannons and open ramparts outside, but the steep stone stairs inside mean a baby carrier beats a stroller.
tips: Walk the ramparts and castle park first, then pop into the castle courtyard playground nearby.

price.note: Main ticket prices not confirmed; temporary-exhibition ticket adult EUR 9, concession EUR 7. A family ticket (up to 2 adults + their children) is available.

discounts: Family ticket (up to 2 adults + their children)
hours: 16 Sep-14 May Wed-Sun 11:00-18:00 (tickets until 17:30); 15 May-15 Sep daily 10:00-18:00
transport: Walk from Kuressaare centre (about 10 min)

name: Kuressaare Castle Courtyard Playground
description: A medieval-themed playground of nearly 800 m² by the castle, opened in 2019, with a separate area designed for children under 3 and another for ages 3-8. It is one of the best toddler playgrounds on Saaremaa and an easy add-on to a castle visit.

price.note: Free.

transport: Next to Kuressaare castle, walk from the centre

name: Kuressaare Town Beach
description: A small town beach right behind the castle and castle park, with a modern children's playground, swings, a sandbox, toilets and changing cabins. The bay is shallow, so a toddler can paddle safely, and you can walk there from the centre with a stroller.
tips: Combine a morning at the castle with a picnic here; there is food service and pedal-boat rental in summer.

price.note: Free.

hours: Open all the time; facilities in summer
transport: Walk from the castle / town centre

name: Angla Windmill Hill and Heritage Centre
description: Saaremaa's iconic row of wooden windmills, with a heritage centre and, in summer, farm animals and birds to meet. The open grounds suit a toddler who likes to run, and preschool children get in free.
tips: Visit May-August if your toddler wants to see the farm animals; the site is about 40 km north of Kuressaare.

price.note: Adult EUR 10, pupil EUR 5, senior/student EUR 7, family EUR 20 (2 adults + children up to 18); preschool children free. Unlimited one-day access.

discounts: Family ticket (2 adults + children up to 18)
transport: By car, about 40 km north of Kuressaare on the Kuressaare-Leisi road

name: Hiiumaa Museum – Long House
description: Hiiumaa's main museum is housed in a 60-metre-long former factory managers' house, with a permanent exhibition aimed largely at small children. It also has the only children's playroom in Kärdla, making it the go-to indoor stop on the island.
tips: Step out the back door into the Beach Park (Rannapark) for a playground and a walk after the museum.

price.note: Prices not confirmed online; check with the museum.

hours: May-Aug daily 10:00-18:00; Sep daily 10:00-17:00; Oct-Apr Mon-Fri 10:00-17:00, Sat 10:00-15:00
transport: Central Kärdla, walk from Keskväljak

name: Kärdla Beach Park
description: A 3.3-hectare park behind the Hiiumaa Museum with a playground next to the song festival grounds, a sandpit and a low ropes adventure trail. It is an easy, free outdoor stop with flat paths for a stroller.
tips: The low ropes trail is for older kids, but toddlers can try the lowest elements with a hand to hold.

price.note: Free.

transport: Central Kärdla, behind the Hiiumaa Museum

name: Kärdla Beach
address: Kärdla rand, near Kärdla harbour, Kärdla
description: A shallow, sandy town beach next to Kärdla harbour with wooden sculptures, a small playground, swings, toilets and changing cabins. At low water little sand islands appear that toddlers love, though the strip of sand is narrow and parts of the shallows are stony.
tips: There is no proper car park, so walk or cycle from the centre (1-2 km) and bring water shoes for the stony patches.

price.note: Free.

transport: 1-2 km from Kärdla centre on foot or by bike

parkingInfo.note: No car park; people leave cars along the road. Walking or cycling is easiest.

name: Narva Castle (Narva Museum)
description: Medieval Hermann Castle on the Narva River, facing Ivangorod fortress across the border, with museum halls in the tower and a castle yard with craft workshops. Toddlers mostly enjoy the courtyard, the walls and the river view; the tower exhibitions have stairs and are better for older children.
tips: Leave the stroller in the courtyard area and carry a baby carrier for the tower; the museum runs family days and Christmas events for children, so check the 'For children' calendar.

price.note: Full ticket 16, discount ticket 10, family ticket 32 (2 adults + their minor children). Castle + Art Gallery combo: 18 / 12 / 36. Children up to 8 free (per official ticket page; confirm at the desk).

discounts: Family ticket (2 adults + their minor children)
Combined ticket with Narva Art Gallery
hours: Summer (11 May-31 Aug) daily 10:00-18:00; off-season Wed-Sat 10:00-18:00, Sun 10:00-16:00 (check, pages differ); ticket sales end 1 h before closing
transport: Walk from Narva city centre / bus station (about 10 minutes)

parkingInfo.note: Street and square parking around Peterburi mnt and Town Hall square next to the castle; check signs for paid hours.

name: Narva River Promenade
address: Narva jõe promenaad, below Narva Castle, Narva
description: A paved, roughly 1 km riverside promenade below the castle walls, with benches and views of Ivangorod fortress. The Swedish terrace section has a family area with lion-shaped play figures, so it works as a free stroller walk with a short play stop.
tips: Combine with Narva Castle and continue north along the river to the Joaoru beach area in summer.

price.note: Free, public promenade.

transport: Walk from Narva centre or Narva Castle

parkingInfo.note: Park near the castle / Town Hall square and walk down to the river.

name: Joaoru Recreation Area and Beach
description: A 17-hectare riverside recreation area that continues the Narva promenade, with a sandy river beach, lifeguard tower, playgrounds and a beach house with changing rooms. It is a good free summer spot for toddlers to dig in the sand and run around on the grass.
tips: The river is next to the state border; stay within the marked bathing area and keep toddlers close to the water's edge.

price.note: Beach and playgrounds free; beach house rents bikes, sunbeds and games for a fee.

hours: Beach season May-August; beach house Mon-Fri 12:00-22:00, Sat 11:00-22:00, Sun 11:00-21:00 (may have changed)
transport: Walk along the river promenade from Narva Castle (about 15-20 minutes)

name: Astri Centre (children's play room)
description: Narva's largest shopping and entertainment centre, with a children's play room alongside a cinema and bowling. Useful as a warm indoor stop on a rainy or freezing day, combined with errands and a café.
tips: The play room's own hours and fees are not published online; call the centre before making a special trip.

price.note: Centre entry free; play room price not published.

transport: City buses along Tallinna mnt

name: Meresuu Spa water and sauna centre
nameLocal: Meresuu Spa & Hotel vee- ja saunakeskus
description: Seaside spa hotel whose water and sauna centre has a children's pool with small attractions and a separate pool for babies. One of the few warm-water options for toddlers in the Narva area.
tips: Day-ticket prices are not published online; call the spa reception and ask about child ages and swim nappies.

price.note: Day-visitor prices not published online; hotel guests have free access.

transport: Bus from Narva to Narva-Jõesuu (about 20 minutes)

parkingInfo.note: Narva-Jõesuu town parking is paid 1 May-30 Sep (5 EUR day ticket, 30 min free with parking clock); hotel parking rules may differ.

name: Narva-Jõesuu Beach
description: A long, fine-sand Gulf of Finland beach with a wooden promenade, a children's playground for climbing, swinging and sand play, changing cabins and an outdoor shower. The shallow, gently sloping water is pleasant for toddlers on warm days.
tips: Bring a sun tent; the pine forest behind the beach offers shade for naps.

price.note: Free public beach.

hours: Open all the time; beach café daily from 11:00 in summer
transport: Bus from Narva to Narva-Jõesuu

parkingInfo.note: Paid town parking 1 May-30 Sep: 30 min free with a parking clock, day ticket 5 EUR (SMS, mobile, card machines); private car parks have their own fees.

name: Sillamäe Seaside Promenade
description: A renovated pedestrian promenade running from the Stalinist-era Mere puiestee down to the sea and along the shore, with several playgrounds, sandboxes, fountains and a small beach with changing rooms. Flat paved paths make it an easy stroller outing with play stops along the way.
tips: Start at the top of Mere puiestee for the grand staircase view, then follow the promenade to the playgrounds by the sea.

price.note: Free.

hours: Open 24 h; fountains in summer only
transport: Buses from Narva or Jõhvi to Sillamäe centre

name: Toila-Oru Park
description: Former summer residence park of President Päts in the Pühajõgi river valley by the sea cliff, managed by RMK, with walking paths, bridges, terraces, a children's playground and picnic spots. Main paths are fine for a stroller, while the steps down to the river and beach are steep.
tips: Use the main entrance car park and stay on the upper paths with a stroller; bring a carrier if you want to go down to the river mouth.

price.note: Free entry.

transport: Bus to Toila from Jõhvi or Kohtla-Järve

parkingInfo.note: Car parks at the park entrances; Toila introduced paid summer parking (from May), check signs.

name: Toila Spa – Toila Termid
description: Seaside spa hotel next to Oru park whose pool and family-oriented 'Toila Termid' sauna centre accept small children, and the hotel also has a play area for kids. Children under 3 go in free, which makes it an inexpensive warm-water outing for toddlers.
tips: Children under 3 must wear swim nappies; weekday daytime (10-16) tickets are the cheapest.

price.note: Under 3 free. Child (4-14) 8-11 EUR depending on day/time and 1.5 h or 3 h ticket. Family 2 adults + 2 children (4-14) 33 EUR on weekday tariff. Adult prices vary by time slot; see price list.

hours: Tariffs: weekdays 10:00-16:00 and 16:00-22:00, Fri-Sun and holidays separate; check exact hours
transport: Bus to Toila from Jõhvi or Kohtla-Järve

name: Estonian Mining Museum (Kohtla Mine Park)
description: Former oil-shale mine where visitors ride a mine train and see real machinery on a 1.5-hour underground tour, plus a kids' exhibition above ground. Children under 4 enter free, but the dark, noisy underground tour suits confident 2-3 year olds best and is too long for many toddlers.
tips: The underground part requires advance booking by phone; bring warm clothes (it is cool underground all year) and a carrier instead of a stroller.

price.note: Underground tour 1.5 h: adult 23, discounted (children, pupils, students, pensioners) about 15, family 60 (2 adults + up to 5 children under 19). Children under 4 free.

discounts: Family ticket (2 adults + up to 5 children under 19)
hours: Tue-Sat 11:00-17:00; underground ticket sales end 2 h before closing; booking required
transport: Car recommended; Kohtla-Nõmme is about 10 km west of Kohtla-Järve

parkingInfo.note: Free car park at the museum.

name: Jõhvi Concert Hall (children's shows)
description: Eesti Kontsert's modern concert hall in Jõhvi, which regularly hosts children's plays and concerts, often on weekend mornings (e.g. 'Pöial-Liisi' on 18 Oct 2026). Short children's shows in the chamber hall are a good first theatre experience for 2-3 year olds.
tips: Check the programme for shows marked 'lasteetendus' and pick morning slots that fit around nap time.

price.note: Ticket prices vary by event; buy via the hall's site or Piletilevi.

hours: Event times vary; box office/administration Mon-Fri 10:00-17:00
transport: Walk from Jõhvi centre; Jõhvi bus and train station nearby

name: Jõhvi Town Park playground
description: Central town park next to the concert hall with a renovated, enlarged playground and a low ropes course under the trees. A free, shady stop that pairs well with a children's show or a walk along the town promenade.
tips: The low ropes course is for older kids; toddlers do better on the main playground equipment.

price.note: Free.

transport: Walk from Jõhvi centre or bus station

parkingInfo.note: Park at the concert hall or in the town centre.

name: Kiviõli Adventure Centre
description: Activity centre on Kiviõli's oil-shale ash hills: a family adventure park with a playground in summer and a ski centre with a 90 m beginner slope and magic-carpet lift in winter. Most attractions target older children, but the playground and beginner slope work for 2-3 year olds with a parent.
tips: In winter, use the magic-carpet beginner area for a first sledge or ski try; the summer park opens around midsummer (20 June in 2026).

price.note: Winter lift/day tickets were about 15-25 EUR for adults and children (2023-24 season); 2026-27 prices not yet confirmed.

hours: Winter: Tue-Thu 12:00-19:00, Fri 12:00-20:00, Sat 10:00-20:00, Sun 10:00-18:00 (school-holiday hours differ); summer park from late June
transport: Car recommended; Kiviõli train station is about 2 km away

name: Rakvere Castle
description: A medieval castle on Vallimägi hill turned into a hands-on 'medieval theme park', with costumed staff, animals, crafts and archery for older kids. Toddlers enjoy the open yard and costumes, though some dark rooms (torture chamber, 'hell') can be scary and stairs are steep.
tips: Skip the dark cellar rooms with a sensitive toddler; the big Tarvas aurochs statue and playground on Vallimägi make a free add-on.

price.note: Adult 13, discount 10, family 27 (up to 2 adults with children). Children up to 8 free. Prices from the 2025 price page; special events cost more.

discounts: Family ticket (up to 2 adults with children)
hours: Summer (Jul-Aug) Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00; Oct-Nov Wed-Sun 10:00-16:00; ticket sales end 1 h before closing
transport: Walk from Rakvere centre (about 10 minutes)

parkingInfo.note: Parking below Vallimägi; Rakvere centre has municipal paid zones.

name: AQVA Water and Sauna Centre
description: Rakvere's spa-hotel water park with pools, slides and saunas; children up to 5 enter free with a paying adult, and there are paid baby swimming sessions. A reliable all-weather option for toddlers in Lääne-Viru county.
tips: Under-5s share the adult's locker; the visitor rules require children under 12 to be supervised by someone at least 16.

price.note: Adult single entry from about 16-20 EUR for 2.5 h depending on time slot; family ticket from 44 (up to 2 adults + 3 children up to 18). Children up to 5 free with a paying adult. Baby swimming 7 EUR.

discounts: Children up to 5 free with paying adult
transport: Walk from Rakvere centre or bus station

name: Hurraa Mängumaa play centre
address: Põhjakeskuse tee 9, Tõrremäe küla, Rakvere vald
description: Indoor play centre in the Põhjakeskus shopping area on the northern edge of Rakvere, with climbing frames, slides and soft play plus birthday rooms. A practical rainy-day option; children under 5 must be accompanied and one accompanying adult goes in free.
tips: Check the site for the staff holiday closure before visiting; overtime is charged per minute, so watch the clock.

price.note: Play ticket 8 EUR for 1 h, 12 for 2 h, 14 for 3 h; overtime 0.05 EUR/min. One accompanying adult free. New prices from 1 Oct 2025.

hours: Tue-Thu 11:00-20:00, Sat-Sun 10:00-21:00 (official site; other listings show Tue-Fri 12:00-21:00); Mon closed
transport: Car or local bus to Põhjakeskus

parkingInfo.note: Free shopping-centre car park.

name: Rakvere Theatre Park playground
address: Rahvaaed / Teatripark, behind Rakvere Theatre (Kreutzwaldi 2a), Rakvere
description: A fenced playground behind Rakvere Theatre next to a pond, with two slides of different heights, a climbing area, sandbox, swings including a baby swing, a spring rider and benches for parents. Being fenced and compact, it is one of the easiest playgrounds in Rakvere for toddlers.
tips: For a newer, bigger option, the Palermo forest playground (2024) at the end of J. Kunderi street sits next to health trails and a sledging hill.

price.note: Free.

transport: Walk from Rakvere centre

parkingInfo.note: Street parking near the theatre; central Rakvere has paid municipal zones.

name: Palmse Manor
description: A restored baroque manor in Lahemaa National Park with a furnished manor house, farm animals, ponds and a large park that is free to walk. Toddlers enjoy the animals and the open park, and the flat gravel paths are manageable with a sturdy stroller.
tips: If the house tour is too much for a toddler, walk the free park and ponds and eat at the Palmse inn (kõrts).

price.note: 1 May-30 Sep: adult 12, student/pensioner 10, family 24 (2 adults with children). 1 Oct-30 Apr: 8 / 7 / 18. Ticket covers the manor house and animals; the park is free.

hours: May-Sep daily 10:00-18:00; Oct-Apr Wed-Sun 10:00-16:00 (check, some pages say Tue-Sun)
transport: Car recommended; about 30 km north-west of Rakvere

name: Sagadi Manor and Forest Museum
address: Sagadi küla, Haljala vald, Lääne-Viru maakond
description: RMK's manor complex in Lahemaa with an interactive forest museum (animal displays, games, a small cinema) and a manor house with a formal park. The animal and nature exhibits hold a toddler's attention, and the cheap family ticket makes it a low-stress stop.
tips: One ticket covers both the forest museum and the manor house; the RMK nature school runs programmes by arrangement.

price.note: Adult 5, student/pensioner 3, family ticket 10 (1-2 adults + children up to 17). One ticket for forest museum, manor house and winter garden.

hours: 1 May-30 Sep daily 10:00-18:00; 1 Oct-30 Apr 10:00-16:00 (one RMK page says Thu-Sun; check)
transport: Car recommended; about 25 km north of Rakvere

name: Võsu Beach
address: Võsu supelrand, Võsu alevik, Haljala vald
description: A long, sandy, shallow bay beach in Lahemaa with lifeguards in summer, changing cabins, toilets, showers and several playgrounds aimed at different ages. The calm shallow water and pine shade make it one of the best toddler beaches in the area.
tips: Use the 30-minute free parking disc only for short stops; for a beach day pay for parking or arrive early.

price.note: Free public beach.

hours: Open all the time; lifeguards in summer season
transport: Bus from Rakvere or Tallinn to Võsu

parkingInfo.note: Võsu village centre parking is paid around the clock 15 May-31 Aug; 30 min free with parking disc at the Rannaklubi car park; free during Rannaklubi events. Car park about 150 m from the sea.

name: Viljandi Castle Ruins (Castle Hills)
description: The ruins of the medieval Order castle sit in a big green park on hills above Lake Viljandi, crossed by a red suspension bridge that toddlers love to walk over. Paths are partly gravel and hilly with steep slopes, so it works best for a short stroller walk or with a carrier.
tips: Combine it with the big lakeside playground below the hills; the walk down is steep, so drive or go round by the road with a stroller.

price.note: Free, open park.

transport: Walk from Viljandi old town centre (about 5 minutes from the main square)

parkingInfo.note: Street parking in the old town near the castle park; check local signs, as central Viljandi has paid zones.

name: Lake Viljandi Beach Playground
address: Viljandi järve rand, Ranna pst, Viljandi
description: A large 2,200 m² sand-covered playground on the shore of Lake Viljandi with swings, slides, climbing frames, a 6 m pyramid and a Tarzan track, split in two by a boardwalk with benches. Some equipment is aimed at older kids, but there are swings and low slides for toddlers, and the beach and swimming area are right next to it.
tips: In summer pair it with a paddle at the beach next door; bring a spade and bucket for the big sand area.

price.note: Free public playground.

transport: About 15 minutes' walk downhill from the old town; car parking by the beach

parkingInfo.note: Parking along Ranna puiestee near the beach and stadium.

name: Viljandi Children's Park
description: A small, quiet park in the town centre with a sandpit, slide, rope climber and swings for little ones, plus granite children's sculptures. It is a handy free stop between errands, but smaller and simpler than the lakeside playground.

price.note: Free public park.

transport: Short walk from Viljandi centre and bus station

name: Pokumaa
address: Padasoomäe talu, Urvaste küla, Antsla vald, 66518 Võru maakond
description: A forest theme park built around Edgar Valter's Poku picture-book characters, with a poku-shaped visitor house, forest paths and play spots. Toddlers who know the Poku books enjoy it most; forest paths are uneven, so a carrier or all-terrain stroller is easier.
tips: Read a Poku book before you go, and allow about 3 hours as the park suggests.

price.note: Family ticket EUR 24 (2 adults + their children, valid in 2026). Older price list: adult 10, child 7, under 3 free. Group rates available.

hours: 20 Jun-25 Aug daily 11:00-18:00; 1 May-19 Jun and 26 Aug-30 Sep Sat-Sun 12:00-16:00; winter by advance booking only
transport: Best by car; about 30 km north-west of Võru

parkingInfo.note: Car park at the park.

name: Lake Tamula Beach and Promenade
description: Võru's town beach on Lake Tamula has a sandy shore, a playground with climbing nets and swings, and an 800 m promenade with benches and swings from Tamula Hotel to Roosisaare bridge. The flat promenade is great for a stroller walk year-round, and toddlers can watch ducks and swans.
tips: The promenade is flat and paved enough for a stroller even outside the swimming season.

price.note: Free public beach.

transport: Walk from Võru centre (about 10 minutes)

parkingInfo.note: Parking near the beach and Tamula Hotel.

name: Suur Munamägi Observation Tower
address: Haanja küla, Rõuge vald, Võru maakond
description: The tower on top of the Baltic states' highest hill has a lift, so you can take a toddler and even a stroller up to the viewing platform above the treetops. The climb from the car park to the tower is a short but steep forest path with steps, so a carrier is easier than a stroller.
tips: Children up to 6 go free; go on a clear day and allow about 45-60 minutes.

price.note: Last seen price list (may be outdated): adult 7, reduced 4 (children 7-18, students, 63+), family 15 (2 adults + children 7-18); children up to 6 free.

hours: Apr-Aug daily 10:00-20:00; Sep-Oct daily 10:00-17:00; Nov-Mar daily 10:00-15:00
transport: By car, about 17 km south of Võru

parkingInfo.note: Car park at the foot of the hill by the Haanja-Rõuge road.

name: Karilatsi Open Air Museum
address: Karilatsi küla, Kanepi vald, Põlva maakond
description: South Estonia's largest open-air museum shows an old village on 5 hectares, with farm buildings, an old schoolhouse and a windmill to wander between. It is calm and spacious for a toddler to explore on foot; grass and gravel paths make a sturdy stroller the better choice.
tips: Ticket sales end an hour before closing; in winter it is open only on weekdays.

price.note: Recent listing: full ticket 6, reduced from 3, family 12 (older listing: 5/2/10).

hours: 1 May-30 Sep Mon-Sun 10:00-18:00; 1 Oct-30 Apr Mon-Fri 10:00-16:00
transport: By car, about 20 km west of Põlva

parkingInfo.note: Car park at the museum.

name: Põlva Sports Centre Swimming Pool
description: The town's indoor pool and saunas are a warm option for a rainy day with a little one. Children up to 6 swim free with a paying adult, which makes a toddler swim cheap.
tips: Weekday daytime (08:00-17:00) tickets were half the evening price in the 2024 list.

price.note: 2024 price list (a new list took effect 1 Jul 2025, figures not confirmed): weekdays 08-17 adult 5 / family 15, evenings and weekends adult 10 / family 24; children up to 6 free with a paying adult.

discounts: Children up to 6 free with an adult
transport: In Põlva town centre, walking distance from the bus station

name: Põlva Lake Beach
description: The renovated town beach on Põlva's dam lake has boardwalks, a swimming jetty, changing cabins and lifeguards in summer, plus a pump track for older kids. Toddlers can dig in the sand and paddle at the edge while you stay in the town centre.
tips: Lifeguards are on duty from 1 June to 31 August.

price.note: Free public beach.

hours: Open all the time; lifeguards 1 Jun-31 Aug
transport: Walk from Põlva centre

name: Wittenstein Time Centre (Paide Vallitorn)
description: A hands-on history centre inside the rebuilt Paide castle tower on Vallimägi hill, where visitors walk through scenes from different eras. It is aimed more at school-age kids, but pre-schoolers get in free, so it is an easy indoor stop with a curious toddler.
tips: Pre-school children are free; after the visit let the toddler run around the grassy castle hill outside.

price.note: Adult 12, pensioner 11, student 9, family 25 (children with parents); pre-schoolers free. Combo ticket with the Activity Museum: adult 19, family 40. Older page shows 8/7/5/17.

discounts: Combo ticket with Wittenstein Activity Museum
hours: Wed-Sun 10:00-18:00 (Jun-Aug daily); 8 Jan-14 Apr by advance booking only
transport: Walk from Paide central square (about 5 minutes)

name: Paide Castle Hill (Vallimägi)
description: The grassy ramparts and castle ruins around the octagonal Vallitorn tower form a free green park right next to Paide centre. Toddlers can roll down the slopes and explore the old walls, but watch for steep drops at the edges.

price.note: Free, open park (the tower's Time Centre is ticketed).

transport: Walk from Paide central square

name: Kallaste Hobby Farm
address: Kallaste, Abaja küla, Järva vald, 73025 Järva maakond
description: A small family farm where children can feed the animals and birds and walk into the enclosures freely, with no time limits. It is a relaxed, hands-on outing for a toddler who loves animals; expect farmyard ground rather than paved paths.
tips: Outside the regular season write or call ahead before driving out.

price.note: May-Sep EUR 7 per person; under 3 free.

hours: May-Sep Tue-Sun 11:00-20:00 (April Thu-Sun); other times by arrangement
transport: By car, near Koeru, about 30 km north-east of Paide

name: Rapla Children's Park
address: Rapla lastepark, Rapla linn, Rapla vald
description: A renovated central playground in a green, quiet corner of town with a sandpit, various swings, climbing frames and slides for both smaller and bigger children. Rubber safety surfacing and CCTV make it a comfortable everyday spot, a short walk from the main square, library and cafés.

price.note: Free public playground.

transport: Walk from Rapla central square

parkingInfo.note: Free parking by the park (not signposted).

name: Rapla Central Square
description: Rapla's main square has a play area, a fountain, seating and a café, and a newer market section with its own children's corner. It hosts family days such as Rapla Melu and Lasteparadiis with carousels and trampolines in season.
tips: Check the Rapla events calendar for family days on the square.

price.note: Free public square.

transport: Rapla town centre

name: Paluküla Mäe Farm
address: Mäe, Paluküla, Kehtna vald, 79019 Rapla maakond
description: A family farm with alpacas, rabbits, chickens and other animals plus a playground with a big swing, net swing, pirate ship, slide and tree house. Visits are by advance booking, so it suits a planned weekend outing or a small birthday rather than a drop-in.
tips: Book ahead; the playground can also be rented separately.

price.note: Farm visit listed at EUR 35 (unclear whether per group); playground rental EUR 25. Confirm when booking.

transport: By car, about 20 km south-east of Rapla

name: Viimsi Open Air Museum
address: Rohuneeme tee 53a, Pringi küla, Viimsi vald
description: A recreated coastal fishing village with old farmhouses, nets and boats, a big swing area and farm animals that small children especially enjoy. It is compact and grassy, good for a toddler to roam; gravel and grass paths are fine with a sturdy stroller.
tips: Check the events calendar; the museum hosts seasonal family days and the Museum of Coastal Folk nearby is free.

price.note: Full ticket 8, discount 5 (children 9-17, students, seniors), family 15. Viimsi residents' annual pass 10. The Museum of Coastal Folk (Nurme tee 3) is free.

hours: May-Sep daily 10:00-19:00; Oct-Apr Wed-Sun 11:00-17:00 (sources differ; check before visiting)
transport: Bus from Tallinn to Pringi/Rohuneeme stops

parkingInfo.note: Car park at the museum.

name: Atlantis H2O Aquapark
description: The water park at Viimsi Spa has slides, wave and play pools and a shallow children's area, all under one roof. Children aged 0-5 get in free with a paying parent, so it is good value for a toddler, though it gets loud and busy at weekends.
tips: Go on a weekday in the school holidays at opening time for a quieter children's pool.

price.note: 3-hour visit from EUR 18 (adult). Children 0-5 free with a parent who bought a ticket (otherwise 0-3 EUR 4, 4-5 EUR 6). Hotel guests 15 EUR/person for the stay.

discounts: Children 0-5 free with a paying parent
hours: Outside summer Fri 14:00-22:00, Sat-Sun 10:00-22:00; summer (8 Jun-31 Aug) and Estonian/Finnish/Latvian school holidays daily from 10:00
transport: Bus from Tallinn to Viimsi (Haabneeme) stops

parkingInfo.note: Car park at Viimsi Spa.

name: Keila Health Centre Swimming Pool
description: Keila's swimming centre has a 25 m pool plus a smaller pool, a slide, jacuzzi and saunas, and an outdoor pool. The small pool suits toddlers, and a child under 3 costs just EUR 1 with a swim nappy.
tips: Children under 10 must be accompanied by someone aged 16 or over; bring a swim nappy.

price.note: Children: 0-3 EUR 1 (with swim nappy), 4-6 EUR 2, 7-12 EUR 3.5. Adult prices not confirmed (2020 list: 3.50-8 depending on time).

transport: Walk from Keila train station or bus station

name: Muumioru Alpaca Farm
address: Muumioru, Tuula küla, 76618 Saue vald, Harju maakond
description: North Estonia's largest alpaca farm, where visitors can meet, feed and pet alpacas and walk the pastures on a guided tour. Toddlers enjoy feeding the gentle animals; children under 2 are free, so it is a short, easy outing from Tallinn.
tips: Weekend opening day differs between pages (Sat or Sun) - check the website before driving out.

price.note: Meet & Feed ticket 15; family ticket 55 (2 adults + 3 children); 13 each when buying 5+ in advance; under 2 free.

hours: Autumn-winter: weekends 12:00-16:00 (Saturday per homepage, Sunday 12:00-15:00 per contact page); other days by booking (min. 5 tickets)
transport: By car, about 30 km south-west of Tallinn

name: Padise Monastery
description: The atmospheric ruins of a medieval Cistercian monastery with a modern visitor centre, towers and vaulted rooms to explore. Older toddlers enjoy the echoing halls and grassy grounds, but there are many stairs and uneven floors, so carry the little one inside.
tips: Tickets are sold at the visitor centre, not in the monastery itself.

price.note: Adult 10, discount 7, family 22; group discounts; guided tours 50 (Estonian) / 70 (foreign language). Older figures 8/5/16 also appear.

hours: May-Sep Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00; Oct-Apr Fri-Sun 11:00-16:00; closed Mondays
transport: By car, about 45 km south-west of Tallinn

name: Nord Sport baby & toddler swimming (Elamus Spa)
nameLocal: Nord Sport beebide ja väikelaste ujumine
description: Weekly group lessons in Elamus Spa's warm children's pool, with a parent in the water for babies and toddlers and coach-led groups from about age 4. Lessons build water confidence through play, songs and games, so they suit families who want a steady weekly class in Mustamäe.
tips: Register online on nordsport.ee; places are taken by monthly subscription, so ask about free spots in the age group before the month starts.

price.note: Monthly fee: 1 lesson/week EUR 58, 2/week EUR 64, 3/week EUR 97 (+ one-off EUR 5.09 registration fee). Check current prices on nordsport.ee.

hours: Weekly lessons on weekdays and weekends; season runs September–May with summer courses
transport: Mustamäe bus/trolley stops near Akadeemia tee

parkingInfo.note: Car park at the spa building.

name: Orca Swim Club baby & toddler swimming
nameLocal: Orca Swim Club beebi- ja väikelaste ujumine
description: Baby classes (4–24 months) and toddler classes (2–4 years) run once a week with a parent in a children's pool of at least 32°C. Orca teaches at Sõle pool in Tallinn and at Järveküla pool in Peetri (Rae vald), handy for families in the southern suburbs.
tips: Register for a group on orca.ee; fees are monthly, and the club's FAQ explains what to bring for the first lesson.

price.note: Monthly fee for 1 lesson/week: EUR 40 at Sõle pool, EUR 48 at Järveküla pool (Reti tee 20, Peetri).

hours: Once a week, weekday and weekend slots; school-year season

parkingInfo.note: Parking at the sports centre.

name: Applied Massage and Therapy College baby swimming
nameLocal: Rakenduslik Massaaži- ja Teraapiakolledž – imikute ja väikelaste ujutamine
description: A small private pool heated to 30°C+, where an experienced children's instructor guides at most two babies with their parents at a time. The very small group makes it a calm first step for young babies and for parents who feel unsure in big public pools.
tips: Book a time by phone or email; parking is free for 2 hours with a parking disc or by registering your car at the front desk. Bring a swim nappy and towel.

price.note: Price not published in search results; ask when booking.

transport: Kadaka tee stops (buses)

parkingInfo.note: Free for 2 hours with a parking disc or by registering your car number with the administrator.

name: West Tallinn Central Hospital baby swimming (Haabersti Health Centre)
nameLocal: Lääne-Tallinna Keskhaigla imikute ja väikelaste ujutamine
description: The hospital's rehabilitation centre runs 30-minute group lessons for babies and toddlers with a parent in a 1.2 m deep pool kept at 32–34°C, with groups split by age. It is a medically run, no-frills option that also offers individual sessions for the smallest babies.
tips: Register by phone (626 1314) or at the health centre reception.

price.note: Price list from 1 Sep 2025: baby pool training EUR 15 per visit; 20-min infant bath session EUR 25.

hours: Weekday group sessions by age group
transport: Õismäe bus stops

parkingInfo.note: Parking at the health centre.

name: Tallinn Viimsi SPA baby swimming
description: Small Monday groups of at most four babies with a parent, led by physiotherapist Svea Miller in the spa's children's pool. The tiny group size suits young babies and families on the Viimsi peninsula.
tips: Pre-register by phone with the coach (+372 5191 8315).

price.note: EUR 13 per child (EUR 11 for club members); price list also shows baby swimming with pre-registration at EUR 15.

transport: Viimsi Keskus / Randvere tee bus stops

name: Päikesetants baby & toddler swimming
description: Group lessons for babies and toddlers with a parent at Nõmme pool, split into beginners and more experienced little swimmers. A long-running Estonian family-activity provider that also offers home bath-swimming sessions.
tips: Beginner babies go to the Tuesday morning groups; the Monday evening group is for babies and toddlers who already have swimming experience. Report absence by email or SMS to the teacher.

price.note: Group prices rose from 10 Oct 2025; see the price list on paikesetants.ee.

transport: Vikerkaare bus stop (buses 14, 18), directly in front of the pool

name: Reval-Sport babies & toddlers swimming
description: 30-minute lessons with a parent in a separate baby pool kept at 32°C (1–1.2 m deep) at a big city-centre sports and water centre. Simple drop-in style cards make it easy to fit around a baby's routine.
tips: Register in the online client portal or by phone (641 2068). Parking in the club yard is free during the lesson if there are spaces.

price.note: Single visit EUR 10; 8-visit card EUR 59 (valid 90 days). Estonian page lists EUR 9 / EUR 56 – check current price.

transport: Viru / Hobujaama stops, city centre

parkingInfo.note: Free in the club yard during the lesson, if spaces are free.

name: Tabasalu Sports Complex baby & toddler swimming
nameLocal: Tabasalu Spordikompleks – beebide ja väikelaste ujumistunnid
description: Thursday morning groups of up to 10 babies with a parent in the children's pool, which is closed to other swimmers during the class. Groups are split into 3–7 months and 8 months–1.5 years, with a mixed-age slot when enough families sign up.
tips: Book a place in advance by phone (+372 5850 9340) or email; a swim nappy is included in the ticket.

price.note: Single ticket (child + parent, swim nappy included) EUR 10; 5 tickets EUR 43.

transport: Tabasalu bus stops (Kooli tn)

name: LaSpa Laulasmaa baby swimming
address: LaSpa, Puhkekodu tee 4, Laulasmaa, Lääne-Harju vald
description: Thursday lessons in the spa's 32–33°C children's and leisure pool, with age groups from 3–6 months up to 1.5–3 years and a parent in the water. A good fit for families in western Harju County, with the seaside spa for a family swim afterwards.
tips: Register with instructor Riin Hiievali by email; lessons are paid monthly, but single visits are possible when there is space.

price.note: Monthly fee (amount not published); single lessons possible if space. Babies 0–12 months visit the water centre free.

name: Lusti baby & toddler swimming (Kurtna)
address: Kurtna lasteaia bassein, Kurtna tee 50, Kurtna, Saku vald
description: Monday morning lessons in a quiet 32–33°C kindergarten pool, with baby groups (3–11 months) and a toddler group (1–3 years) with a parent. The small, calm pool suits babies who find big public pools too loud or chlorinated.
tips: Enter from the back of the kindergarten through the glass door by the car park and go down to the basement pool. Trial lessons only when places are free.

price.note: Monthly package 4 lessons EUR 42; single/trial lesson EUR 13 when places are free.

hours: Mondays from 21 Sep 2026: 9:00, 9:30, 10:30 babies; 10:00 toddlers (30-minute lessons)

parkingInfo.note: Car park behind the kindergarten.

name: SK Fortuna baby swimming (Jüri)
address: Jüri spordihoone, Laste tn 3, Jüri, Rae vald
description: Weekly baby groups (3–7 months and 8–18 months) with a parent in the 31–32°C children's pool of Jüri sports building. A convenient option for families in Rae parish; the club also runs baby groups in Kose.
tips: Register through the club website's registration page; registration for 2026/2027 is open.

price.note: EUR 39 per month (Jüri groups).

hours: Weekly lessons during the school year
transport: Jüri bus stops

name: Aura Centre baby & toddler swimming
nameLocal: Aura Keskus – beebide ja väikelaste ujutamine
description: Coach-led drop-in classes in Tartu's main water centre: 30-minute baby swimming (up to about 2 years) and 40-minute toddler swimming for ages 2–4, both with a parent in the water. Babies learn to float on their back and tummy and go under water, and no advance booking is needed.
tips: Just turn up – no registration needed. Check the current timetable on aurakeskus.ee, as the schedule changes between summer and the school year.

price.note: Baby swimming EUR 9, toddler swimming EUR 10 per lesson (prices from 1 Aug 2026).

hours: Several weekday morning classes (e.g. Mon 10:15); see the timetable
transport: Turu / Aura bus stops, city centre

parkingInfo.note: Paid city-centre parking around the centre.

name: Medicum Tartu baby swimming
description: Physiotherapist-led baby swimming in 32–34°C water at the children's rehabilitation clinic (formerly Babysport), from the second month of life, with one parent in the water and groups by age. Available with a doctor's referral or as a paid service, so it suits babies who need extra support with muscle tone.
tips: Book through the clinic registry by phone or email; physiotherapist-led swimming requires a minimum child weight of 7 kg, and there are also family swim sessions.

price.note: Current price not found; available with a referral or as a paid service.

transport: Annelinn bus stops

name: Beebipuut baby swimming at Arena sports club
description: Small morning groups for babies of about 2–8 months and 9 months–1.5 years with a parent, in Arena's 31°C children's pool. Run by the Tartu baby and pregnancy yoga studio Beebipuut, with online booking per lesson.
tips: Book and pay each lesson online via the Beebipuut timetable; cancel up to 2 hours before, and join the waiting list if full. No lessons in June–August.

price.note: Single lesson EUR 14.10 + EUR 0.94 booking fee; paid by bank transfer when booking.

name: Babyfloat baby spa & swimming
description: A baby spa where specialists guide babies floating in individual mini-tubs, plus group and family baby swimming sessions in a pool. It suits the youngest babies, before they are ready for a public pool.
tips: Book online (SumUp / Veebiregistratuur) or by phone; weekends are by booking only.

price.note: Booking listing (not confirmed on official site): group pool baby swimming 45 min EUR 25, family session EUR 45, mini-tub group EUR 24, private EUR 38.

name: Orca Swim Club baby & toddler swimming (Pärnu)
nameLocal: Orca Swim Club beebi- ja väikelaste ujumine Pärnus
description: Weekly baby (4–24 months) and toddler (2–4 years) lessons with a parent at the city's Raja kindergarten pool. One of the few organised baby-swimming options in Pärnu.
tips: Register for a group on orca.ee; Raja pool closes over the summer, so courses follow the school year.

price.note: Raja baby/toddler swimming EUR 30 or 40 per month (price list does not make clear which is which).

hours: Once a week during the school year

name: Gold Swim baby & toddler swimming (Kohtla-Järve)
nameLocal: Ujumisklubi Gold Swim – beebid ja väikelapsed
description: Parent-and-child groups for 0–2 and 2–4 year olds in a small 32°C pool at the Wiru sports centre. Gold Swim is one of the few clubs in Ida-Viru County running regular baby and toddler swimming.
tips: Call or email the club to join a group and confirm current times.

price.note: Kohtla-Järve groups from EUR 70 per month (not confirmed for the baby group).

name: AQVA Spa baby swimming
description: Weekly baby swimming classes in the water centre's baby and children's pool, in groups for 0–1 and 1–2 year olds with a parent. The 2026/2027 season started on 14 September 2026.
tips: Ask the water centre for the current timetable and how to sign up (+372 326 0010).

price.note: Price not published in search results; ask the water centre.

hours: Last season: Mon & Wed, 0–1 y at 11:00, 1–2 y at 12:00 (confirm for 2026/27)

name: Suure-Jaani Health House baby swimming
description: Weekly 30-minute baby swimming sessions with a parent at a small-town water centre, with a beginners' group and a group for babies who have finished the beginner course. The nearest organised baby swimming we found for Viljandi County families.
tips: Advance booking by phone (432 8124) is required; no classes during school holidays.

price.note: One visit (2 h incl. 30-min baby swimming) EUR 8; 10-visit card EUR 59 (valid 90 days).

name: Kullo Toddler School (4-year-olds)
description: A weekly half-day morning group at Tallinn's municipal hobby centre Kullo where 4-year-olds draw, make crafts, sing and move together without a parent. It suits children who are ready for a short group session away from mum or dad and gently prepares them for the 5- and 6-year-old pre-school groups.
tips: Register through the city's LAUR hobby-school system or Kullo's website; the school year runs September to May and places fill in spring for the next year.

price.note: Monthly fee; the 2024 page listed EUR 45/month (check the 2026/27 rate). Kullo hobby groups in general cost EUR 26-118/month.

discounts: Paid hobby-school fees may qualify for an income tax refund

name: Talveunistus Skating School
description: A figure-skating school at Tondiraba Ice Hall that takes complete beginners from age 3, with a special first-year group for 3-5-year-olds who learn to stand, fall safely and glide through games. Children are on the ice with a coach while parents watch from the stands, so it suits confident pre-schoolers rather than clingy toddlers.
tips: The first two training sessions are free; register on the school's website and bring warm clothes, gloves and a helmet.

price.note: 2025/26: beginners aged 3-5 (first year) EUR 85/month for 2 sessions a week; other groups from EUR 60/month for 1 session a week. Place fee EUR 45 for a missed month.

discounts: 50% sibling discount (2+ skaters from one family)
Income tax refund on fees (licensed school)
hours: Weekday afternoons and weekends at Tondiraba; season September-May
transport: Bus to Tondiraba / Varraku area, Lasnamäe

parkingInfo.note: Large car park at the ice hall.

name: Rocca al Mare Skating School
description: A long-running skating school at Haabersti Ice Hall that welcomes children from age 3 all year round, combining ice sessions with an off-ice general-fitness class. The youngest skaters learn basic balance and gliding in small groups with a coach while parents wait by the rink; there is also a Russian-language page.
tips: The first two trial sessions are free; apply via the registration form on the website.

price.note: Monthly: EUR 90 (1 ice session + 1 off-ice), EUR 120 (2 + 1), EUR 150 (3 + 1). Paid at the school office on the rink's 2nd floor.

discounts: Income tax refund on fees (licensed school)
hours: All year; weekday afternoons and Saturdays at Haabersti Ice Hall
transport: Rocca al Mare / Haabersti stops (buses), Paldiski mnt

parkingInfo.operator: Haabersti Ice Hall / Rocca al Mare area
parkingInfo.note: Parking by the ice hall, next to Rocca al Mare shopping centre.

name: Infonet Football School (kids' football from 3)
description: A large Tallinn football school whose youngest groups start at age 3 with playful running, ball and coordination games rather than real matches. Training is mainly in Russian, with toddler groups held in several districts (Lasnamäe, Õismäe, Kopli, Mustamäe), outdoors in summer and in sports halls in winter.
tips: New children get a free trial session and a club T-shirt; ask which district hall is nearest for the 3-5-year-old group.

price.note: City listing: EUR 85-105/month depending on group (may be outdated; confirm current fee).

hours: Weekday afternoons/evenings; outdoors in summer, indoor halls in winter

name: Arigato Baby & Toddler Gymnastics
description: Parent-and-child gymnastics at the Arigato sports club, run by coaches from Tsirkusekool, with separate Saturday groups for babies (3 months-1 year) and toddlers (1-3 years). Parents stay on the mat and help their child roll, crawl, climb and balance on soft equipment; older children up to 7 can continue in acrobatics groups.
tips: Contact the coach Vello Vaher by phone or email to reserve a place; Saturday groups fill fastest.

price.note: Price not published online; ask the coach or Arigato club (club trial session EUR 5).

parkingInfo.note: Car park at the sports club.

name: Noor Ballett Fouetté Ballet Studio (3-6 y)
description: A ballet school's studio group for 3-6-year-olds: a short weekly class of music, movement and first ballet positions, taught without the parent in the room. It is a gentle, no-audition introduction to classical dance for pre-schoolers who enjoy music and dressing up.
tips: Admission to the 3-6 studio groups runs from mid-August to the end of September without auditions; apply by email.

price.note: 2026/27: EUR 65/month for one class a week.

name: Kaie Kõrb Ballet Studio
address: Hobujaama 12, Tallinn (classes at several venues in Tallinn, Viimsi and Peetri)
description: A children's ballet studio founded by former prima ballerina Kaie Kõrb, taking pupils from age 4 in many locations around Tallinn, Viimsi and Rae parish. Classes teach posture, musicality and basic ballet steps in small groups, ending each year with a stage show the children love.
tips: The first lesson is free for new pupils; pick the venue closest to you (city centre, Haabersti, Viimsi Huvikeskus, Viimsi Artium or Peetri).

price.note: Per year: EUR 460 (1 class/week) or EUR 660 (2/week); or 9 monthly payments of EUR 65 / EUR 85 (2025/26 price list).

name: Väike Muusik Baby & Toddler Music Studio
description: Weekly parent-and-child music classes at Nõmme Culture Centre in three age groups (6-11 months, 1-1.5 years and 1.5-2.5 years): singing, rhythm games, small instruments and movement. Each 30-minute lesson is followed by 20 minutes of free play, so it is a relaxed way for babies and parents to meet others.
tips: Book through Nõmme Kultuurikeskus; groups are small, so register early in the autumn.

price.note: EUR 34/month (one lesson a week).

hours: Weekday mornings, three age-group slots; 30 min lesson + 20 min free play
transport: Nõmme train station / Nõmme turg bus stops

parkingInfo.note: Parking around Turu plats in Nõmme centre.

name: Mamma Mia Baby Rhythm & Movement Class
nameLocal: Mamma Mia Beebikooli rütmika- ja liikumistund
description: A 30-minute rhythm, song and movement class for 1-3-year-olds with a parent at the Mamma Mia singing studio in Peetri, just outside Tallinn. Groups are kept to 6-10 children, which suits families in Rae parish and south-east Tallinn looking for a calm first group activity.
tips: Buy a 5-class card if you plan to attend regularly; check the studio's timetable page for the current day and time.

price.note: Single class EUR 10; 5-class card EUR 50 (valid 3 months).

hours: Weekday mornings (previously Tuesdays 10:00); check the 2026/27 timetable

parkingInfo.note: Parking at the Peetri centre.

name: Laula ja kasva Music Circle
description: An early-childhood music circle led by a music therapist for parents with babies and toddlers up to 3: lullabies, nursery songs, simple instruments and movement games. Small, registration-only groups make it a gentle option for families in Keila and western Harju County.
tips: Places are limited and advance registration is required; the first lesson is free for newcomers.

price.note: Monthly membership EUR 15-20 (3 or 4 lessons in the month) + EUR 7 per lesson attended; single drop-in EUR 15. First lesson free. An older page lists a 4-lesson card at EUR 35.

hours: Tuesday and Thursday mornings at 10:00; new season from September

name: Viimsi Hobby Centre Baby & Toddler Gymnastics
nameLocal: Viimsi Huvikeskus beebide ja väikelaste võimlemine
description: Monday-morning gymnastics for babies and toddlers with a parent at Viimsi Hobby Centre, split into 2-7-month, 7-15-month and 1-2-year groups. The instructor shows age-appropriate exercises and movement games that support rolling, crawling and walking, with the parent doing everything together with the child.
tips: Book a trial lesson via the registration link on the hobby centre's page; the 4-class card is valid for 2 months.

price.note: Trial lesson EUR 10; single lesson EUR 15; 4-class card EUR 45 (valid 2 months).

hours: Mondays 9:00 (7-15 months), 10:00 (1-2 years), 11:00 (2-7 months); from September

parkingInfo.note: Free parking at the Viimsi Huvikeskus / school area.

name: Vimka Ski School (little skiers 3+)
address: Randvere tee 30, Lubja küla, Viimsi vald
description: The ski school at Viimsi's small downhill park, the closest slope to Tallinn, offers playful snow sessions for children from age 3 on a gentle learning slope. For the youngest it is more about getting used to skis and moving on snow than real technique, which is exactly right for a first try.
tips: Book lessons online once the slope opens (usually January, snow permitting) and bring a helmet; equipment can be rented on site.

price.note: Little-ones' (3+) group lessons were listed at EUR 9 per session or 5 sessions for EUR 45; small-group lessons (2-3 children) EUR 40 per person / 50 min, plus EUR 5 equipment. Check the current season's price list.

hours: Winter season only, when there is snow; weekends and some weekday afternoons

parkingInfo.note: Car park at the hill.

name: CFC Ski School (Jaak Mae Ski School)
description: Cross-country skiing school run by Olympic medallist Jaak Mae's club, with a group for 4-6-year-olds that trains all year: running and ball games in autumn, skiing in Pirita when there is snow. Coaches keep it playful, so it suits active pre-schoolers who like being outdoors.
tips: There is a free trial week; register on cfc.ee and ask the coach which days the 4-6 group meets.

price.note: 4-6-year-old group EUR 40/month (children's page); general ski-school fee EUR 50/month. Invoiced monthly.

discounts: Income tax refund on training fees
hours: Weekday afternoons all year; on snow in winter

parkingInfo.note: Parking at Pirita Spordikeskus.

name: Piruett Gymnastics Club - dance gymnastics 4-6 y
description: A gymnastics club whose youngest 'dance gymnastics' groups (from 4 years) mix basic gymnastics, stretching and dance to music. There are no entry tests, so it suits any active pre-schooler; groups also run in Jüri (Rae Spordikeskus) and Aruküla.
tips: A free trial session is offered; a one-off EUR 10 joining fee applies when you sign up.

price.note: Around EUR 80-90/month for the 4-6 and 5-6-year-old groups (2025/26); EUR 10 joining fee.

hours: Weekday mornings (e.g. Tue 10:30) and afternoons; school year September-May

name: Kinderdom Children's Studio
description: A small development studio in Lasnamäe with a 'Beebikool / Music with mum' group for 9 months to 2.5 years, plus art-therapy and sensory play, Estonian and English for little ones. Lessons are short (30-45 minutes) with free play afterwards, and the studio works with Russian-speaking as well as Estonian families.
tips: Book individual sessions through the studio's Setmore booking page; message on Instagram or by phone for the group timetable.

price.note: Baby music group EUR 10 per 30-min session (+15 min free play); individual English 45 min EUR 25.

hours: Weekday mornings and afternoons by timetable

name: Pingu's English Tallinn (English for kids 3+)
description: An English-language school for young children using the play-based Pingu's English method: small groups learn through songs, games, stories and the Pingu characters, with the teacher speaking only English. It suits families who want their pre-schooler to pick up English early; the same organisation runs English pre-schools in Kadriorg and Rocca al Mare.
tips: Contact the school for a trial lesson and the current course timetable; courses follow the school year.

price.note: Course price not published; ask the school. (Half-day English pre-school at Rocca al Mare from EUR 185/month for 1 day a week.)

hours: Weekday afternoons; courses follow the school year

name: Fysiongel Baby & Toddler Movement Classes
description: Physiotherapist-led movement classes for babies and young toddlers with a parent, in small groups sorted by developmental stage (youngest babies, first movements, crawlers). It is a good fit if you want gentle, expert guidance on motor development and a chance to ask a physiotherapist questions.
tips: Book ahead on the Fysiongel website; ask which of the three Monday groups matches your child's stage.

price.note: EUR 15 per class; monthly card EUR 50.

name: Akros Gymnastics Club - toddler & parent gymnastics
description: Drop-in toddler gymnastics at Tartu's big gymnastics club: children from 1 year run, jump, climb and roll on mats, trampolines and soft blocks, with a parent or carer joining under-7s. Only the child pays and no pre-registration is needed, which makes it an easy weekend outing.
tips: No pre-registration needed; check the club's timetable for the Tuglase 14 and NET hall sessions.

price.note: 2025/26: EUR 10 per visit for non-members, EUR 6 for Akros members; parent/carer free (paid only for children from 1 year).

hours: Several sessions a week incl. weekends; see timetable

name: Karlova Beebipill Baby Music Group
description: A friendly community music group in Karlova where parents sing and play simple instruments with babies (0-2) and toddlers (2-4). With several weekly slots and a low monthly fee it is one of the easiest regular baby activities in Tartu.
tips: Register by email; daytime slots on Tuesdays and Wednesdays are for 0-2-year-olds, evening slots on Wednesdays for 2-4-year-olds.

price.note: EUR 21/month.

name: Tartu Nature House - Nature Adventurers club
description: A nature club for 3-7-year-olds at Tartu's Nature House, where children explore the house's park, animals and plants through play and short outdoor discoveries. Children attend without a parent in age-based groups, and a child must have turned 3 before starting.
tips: Register for the school year via the Nature House website; preschool sessions last 60 minutes once a week.

price.note: EUR 30/month.

hours: Weekday afternoons, once a week (see timetable); school year September-May

name: Tartu Skating School
address: Lõunakeskus ice rink, Ringtee 75 / Teaduspargi 4, Tartu
description: Tartu's figure-skating club trains at the Lõunakeskus rinks and has a preparatory group for 3-5-year-olds who are just starting out. Little skaters learn balance and gliding through games with a coach on the ice, and the club's own skate shop in Lõunakeskus helps fit proper skates.
tips: Ask about the preparatory (ettevalmistav) group by email or phone; buy properly fitted skates from the start.

price.note: Youngest group EUR 85/month (club group info).

hours: Weekday afternoons on the ice and in the arena's small hall; season September-May

parkingInfo.note: Free parking at Lõunakeskus shopping centre.

name: Tähtvere Dance Centre - pre-school dance
description: Tartu's large dance centre in Tähtvere takes children from age 3 into once-a-week pre-school dance groups built around music, rhythm and simple dance games. It is a good stepping stone into folk, modern or ballroom dance later, and children dance without parents in the room.
tips: Sign up for the autumn term on the website; a one-off joining fee and small annual fee apply on top of the monthly fee.

price.note: 2025/26: pre-school dance EUR 33/month (1x week) or EUR 43 (2x week); joining fee EUR 15, then EUR 8/year.

name: Laulupesa Baby & Toddler Singing Groups
description: A children's singing studio with its own play room, running baby and toddler singing groups in age bands from about 3-8 months up to 2-3 years. Parents sing, bounce and play along with their child, and missed lessons can be swapped for time in the studio's play room.
tips: Check the online timetable for your child's age band and email to join; missed lessons can be used for play-room visits.

price.note: Baby singing group around EUR 20/month (older listing); confirm current fees on the price page.

hours: Weekday mornings by age group (see timetable)

name: Pärnu Old Town Training Centre Baby School
description: A central Pärnu baby school with groups for 6-12-month-olds and walkers aged 1-3: a weekly music lesson plus an optional creative session with painting, sticking and modelling. Parents take part with their child, so it is a gentle introduction to group activities.
tips: Register by phone or email before the autumn term; the creative group can be combined with music at a combined monthly price.

price.note: 1-3-year-olds: about EUR 32-35/month for music; music + creative session about EUR 57/month (older price lists; confirm).

hours: Weekday mornings (music Mondays, art Wednesdays for walkers)

name: Pärnu Sports Academy Kalev - mini tennis from 3
description: Pärnu's sports academy runs 'blue ball' mini-tennis groups for children from about 3-4 years, using soft balls, small rackets and lots of running and catching games. Groups of 8-12 children train twice a week without parents on court, which suits energetic pre-schoolers.
tips: Contact the academy before the autumn term; check whether your child fits the 3-4 or 4-6 blue-ball group (the site lists both age 3 and 4 as the start).

price.note: Ages 3-4 (blue ball): EUR 70-80/month for 2 x 45 min a week.

hours: Weekday afternoons, twice a week; school year September-May

name: Pääsuke Figure Skating Club
description: Narva's figure-skating club trains at the city ice hall and takes beginners from about age 5, with coaching mainly in Russian. It suits older pre-schoolers who already enjoy public skating and want to learn properly; the club also hosts the annual Narva Spring competition.
tips: Ask about beginner intake via the club website or the Narva Paemurru sports school, which runs the ice hall.

price.note: Fees not published online; ask the club.

hours: Weekday afternoons at Narva Ice Hall; season September-May

name: Kuutsemäe Ski School
address: Kuutsemäe suusakeskus, Arula küla, Otepää vald
description: One of Estonia's main downhill ski centres near Otepää, whose ski school offers separate playful snow sessions for little ones from age 3. Children under 7 ski free on the slope with an adult holding a valid lift ticket, so a family first-skiing weekend is affordable.
tips: Book ski-school lessons online ahead of winter weekends and school holidays; helmets are compulsory for all pupils.

price.note: Private lesson EUR 45 / 50 min (1 person), EUR 80 / 1 h 40 min; lift card needed (EUR 6 if you don't have one). Under-7s ski free with an adult who has a valid lift ticket.

discounts: Under-7s free on the slopes with a ticketed adult
hours: Winter season (usually December-March), daily when the slopes are open

parkingInfo.note: Car park at the ski centre.
